newsitem.title: GERMANY: German prisoners on sixth day of hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: German prisoners on sixth day of hunger strike.

text.p: About 50 prisoners at a Frankfurt remand centre on Tuesday marked the sixth day of a hunger strike in protest at what they say are cramped, dirty conditions and inadequate visiting hours.

Ekkehard Hoffmann, director of the Preungesheim centre near Frankfurt, said he agreed with prisoners that cells were overcrowded, but rejected their demands for weekend visits saying he did not have enough staff.
He also dismissed complaints that conditions were unhygienic.
"There are just too many people inside this centre," Hoffmann told reporters. He said the remand prison, which was built to detain 550 people, was currently holding almost 800 people awaiting trial.
Hoffman said that of 254 prisoners who went on hunger strike last Thursday about 50 were still refusing food.
He said a committee of prison representatives would meeting inmates in an attempt to persuade the prisoners to call off their protest.
The prisoners went on hunger strike last Thursday to press their demands for longer visiting hours, better social and medical care and for their time spent remanded in custody to be shorter.
